input.rationale: Reproduction question for the verify probe: the cited receipt b02d5ff23a504a8ea38116085ba8e23c carries a recorded limitation that repeatability of its timing-sensitive control is not established, because that run's no-peer partition stepped down at 202ms against a 200ms lease and its non-voter partition returned success in 0ms. This update re-executes the fixed experiment d704b04e706144dc964ff451359eda19-experiment unchanged and in a clean copy, so the second receipt can be compared with the first on the same three partitions: whether the non-voter-only partition still returns success, whether the voter-only control still succeeds, whether the no-peer partition still fails, and how the lease-driven step-down timing compares. Nothing in the account is claimed until that receipt exists; the current interpretations and knowledge are left unchanged.

Source reads made this turn found no defect to register: the Restore path's commit-ahead behaviour is explicitly documented as disaster-recovery-only, and replication falls back to sending a snapshot on ErrLogNotFound, so a lagging follower is not fed stale or hole-crossing log entries.

fixed_experiment.revision_reason: The previous harness emitted CA_EVENT objects without an event name, so the controller rejected all three as invalid_observation and no observation could be interpreted. This revision only changes the observation format: each case now emits a named assurance_partition_setup event before the partition and a named assurance_verify_leader_result event afterwards, carrying the same measured fields, and declares the setup event as a prerequisite admission with one comparison per partition case.
